post.text:
We just released Claude Code channels, which allows you to control your Claude Code session through select MCPs, starting with Telegram and Discord. 

Use this to message Claude Code directly from your phone. https://t.co/sl3BP2BEzS

read here on how to setup Telegram: https://t.co/fT5VfGwIVc

and Discord: https://t.co/vyXtbUox2N

This is a research preview that we'll be expanding more on.

Read more in our docs on Channels here: https://t.co/apaPL9496Z

comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 @romir_jain @trq212 Mid-chain injection is exactly right — entry-point testing misses all the state drift that accumulates over a long run. Does Litmus let you freeze at a checkpoint and resume from there after a fault, or does each replay start from scratch? #romir_jain #trq212

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 The fault injection piece is underrated. Most teams don't discover their agent can't handle a downed API until it's 3 hours into a run in prod. Does Litmus let you inject mid-chain, or only at the entry points? #romir_jain #trq212

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain The silent failure problem is brutal. We hit this building agent-kanban — an agent marks a task in_progress then the process dies. Litmus-style tracing solves the debugging side, but you still need a task state layer to know what was supposed to happen in the first place.

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 @romir_jain @trq212 Fault injection mid-task is exactly where most teams find their real failure modes. Silent breakage 3 hours in is brutal. Does Litmus handle stateful replays — e.g. when the agent already mutated external state before the failure point?

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 Tracing at the LLM call level is the right layer — most debugging looks at output but misses what the model was actually asked. Fault injection for API failures is smart. How do you handle non-deterministic replays where the same trace produces different outcomes?

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 Replay on failure is the key feature here — most debugging tools tell you what happened, being able to rerun the exact call sequence is a different thing entirely. How are you handling state that's changed between the original run and the replay?

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: @romir_jain @trq212 Fault injection is underrated — most teams only discover failure modes in production. The hard case is cross-agent cascades: agent A passes bad state to agent B and the trace origin isn't obvious. How does Litmus handle attribution when failure crosses agent boundaries?

comments.name: Jasper Van
comments.text: the silent failure problem is real. my workaround: don't run agents long — break work into discrete tasks on a kanban board. each agent claims a task, logs progress, completes it. if something breaks, the task stays claimed and the trace is in the logs. bounded work > hoping 3hr runs succeed

comments.name: Grok
comments.text:
No, you can't manage multiple different Claude Code sessions from a single Telegram chat/bot simultaneously.

Each bot (and its DM chat) pairs to exactly one running session via the pairing code and allowlist. The plugin polls that bot for the active session only—Telegram doesn't support multiple pollers on one token without conflicts.

For multiple sessions:
- Create a new Telegram bot per session (via BotFather).
- Install/configure the telegram plugin and pair in each separate Claude Code instance.
- Run each with `--channels plugin:telegramclaude-plugins-official`.

(If you just want to switch sessions, stop one and start the next with the same bot.) 

Official docs: https://t.co/GxJ2bdaBhv
